Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE original, polished but modestly detailed tower-defense VIDEO GAME SCREENSHOT CONCEPT, landscape 3:2. Must look like an authored game with an integrated bespoke HUD, NOT an HTML website, not dashboard, not rectangles of plain background with text, not a generic beige panel theme. Render the FULL game viewport edge to edge. Distinctive control silhouettes, physical/graphic materials and visual hierarchy appropriate to the specific style below.
COMMON DESIGN CONSTRAINTS: daylight/bright mid-tone environment. Large main battlefield occupying left~76% of top~75%; equipment management occupying right~24% of top; generous vocabulary question interaction across entire bottom~25%. Map has a long clearly continuous winding route, at least40 visible tile-equivalent steps, multiple hairpins and returns, broad buildable regions between passes. Whole map visible. No always-visible checkerboard. Seven large recognizable towers, each exactly centered in a single subtle square build socket, bases comfortably inside socket. Eleven enemy creatures along route with individual running/hopping poses, not evenly spaced. A few short visible projectile trails originate at tower muzzles; ONE small impact burst next to an enemy. Show varied poses, no huge magic effects. Towers and enemies use stylized medium-simple 2D game art, 2-3 shading planes, NO ornate gold fantasy bases or tiny detailed texture, NO flat generic geometric placeholder icons.
Static scenery: several natural trees/shrubs/rocks in nonbuildable clusters, one small peaceful stone memorial stele with a single Hangul letter '가' and one small book monument in a garden corner. The Hangul motif belongs ONLY to these fixed scenery pieces. Absolutely NO alphabet/book/brush/Korean-king themed attacking towers or enemies. Combat units are entirely defined by the genre below. The monuments are not towers, have no health bars, not hit or attacked. Do not copy any existing game or brand.
HUD: top compact lives/hearts, coins and wave badge, pause gear; do NOT add a website title/navigation. Right equipment controls feature 3 large illustrated tower-selection icons, selected unit portrait, compact upgrade/sell action shapes integrated into style; no long descriptive paragraphs, no repeated web cards. Lower question area has a graphic question marker and readable exact Korean sentence "'신중하다'의 뜻은?" plus four LARGE answer controls with Korean texts: '조심스럽게 행동하다', '몹시 서두르다', '힘이 매우 세다', '소리가 매우 크다'. All answers equal neutral status (no preselected correct answer). The lower panel must be generous and legible. Korean fonts are bold/clean game UI. Typography is supported by deliberate iconography, framing, tactility and grouping, not floating text on a blank sheet. Avoid SaaS cards, glassmorphism, excessive gradients, pill badge spam, flat generic web layout. Avoid overly dark lighting and washed-out pastel. This is an original genre direction, NOT a recoloring of the previous direction.
SPECIFIC ART AND UI DIRECTION: Cheerful 2D adventure tactics. Chunky rounded hand-inked sprites: a small green-cloaked archer on a short timber platform, a broad iron cannon, a blue elemental mage. Red goblins and armored boars. Grass landscape with irregular dirt path, low stone walls and clumped pines. UI built from a compact adventurer equipment chest: tower choices in recessed wood sockets with copper corner pins; selected tower portrait in a shield silhouette; bottom question appears on a broad framed field-map folio with 4 chunky carved wood answer keys. Small blue pennants and ruby heart sockets. Broad planes and restrained detail. No parchment wallpaper. Main colors emerald, cobalt, warm ochre, ivory.
